articles.body_raw:
PARIMAL DABHI
AHMEDABAD, JUNE 13

THE DAY after Air India’s
London-bound Al 171 crashed
soon after taking off from
Ahmedabad, staff at the BJ
Medical College, where the air-
craft fell and broke into pieces,
ushered a solemn group of peo-
ple into a large hail on the
ground floor of the main build-
ing and seated them on rows of
benches where the students
usually write their exams.
This was a test of a different

These were family members
and relatives of many of the 241
passengers and crew who had
died in Thursday's crash —arriv-
ing from different parts of the
country, waiting to provide their
DNA samples so that they could
identify whatever was left of
their loved ones,
According to rescue person-
nel, most of the bodies were
charred beyond recognition, and
many died with their seatbelts
stillon.
articles.headline: The day after, the agonising hours: Families line up for DNA tests to identify kin
articles.text:
THE DAY after Air India's London-bound Al 171 crashed soon after taking off from Ahmedabad, staff at the BJ Medical College, where the aircraft fell and broke into pieces, ushered a solemn group of people into a large hail on the ground floor of the main building and seated them on rows of benches where the students usually write their exams. This was a test of a different

These were family members and relatives of many of the 241 passengers and crew who had died in Thursday's crash - arriving from different parts of the country, waiting to provide their DNA samples so that they could identify whatever was left of their loved ones, According to rescue personnel, most of the bodies were charred beyond recognition, and many died with their seatbelts stillon.

articles.body_raw:
SUKALP SHARMA
& RITU SHARMA
NEW DELHI, AHMEDABAD,
JUNE 13

ONE OF the black boxes of the Air
India Boeing 787-8 aircraft has
been recovered from the crash
site in Ahmedabad by the on-site
team of the Aircraft Accident
Investigation Bureau (AAIB),
which is leading the investiga-
tion into the worst aviation dis-
aster involving an Indian airline
in decades.

BUSINESS AS USUAL

By UNNY

PM to families
at hospital
articles.body_raw:
EXPRESS NEWS SERVICE
AHMEDABAD, JUNE 13

PRIME MINISTER Narendra
Modi reached Ahmedabad on
Friday and met the relatives of
those killed and the lone sur-
vivor in the Air India plane crash
the day before, and chaired a “re-
view meeting” with Gujarat
Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel,
state and Central ministers, and
senior officials.
He also met the medical stu-
dents who were injured at the site
ofcrashin BJ Medical College and
currently undergoing treatment
at the Ahmedabad Civil Hospital.
Those he met during the day in-
cluded Anjaliben, wife of Gujarat
ex-CM Vijay Rupani who was
among the 241 who died in the
crash in Meghaninagar.
CONTINUED ON PAGE 2
articles.headline: Difficult time, stay strong: PM to families at hospital
articles.text: PRIME MINISTER Narendra Modi reached Ahmedabad on Friday and met the relatives of those killed and the lone survivor in the Air India plane crash the day before, and chaired a "review meeting" with Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, state and Central ministers, and senior officials. He also met the medical students who were injured at the site ofcrashin BJ Medical College and currently undergoing treatment at the Ahmedabad Civil Hospital. Those he met during the day included Anjaliben, wife of Gujarat ex-CM Vijay Rupani who was among the 241 who died in the crash in Meghaninagar.
